_: THE HOUSE FORM FOR THE -youtube.txt FILE. ONE HOME, READ BY BOTH SIDES.
__: The file a human pastes the YouTube description from carries THREE things: the
decided title on line 1, the DESCRIPTION, and the NOTES (sources, hashtag reasoning,
anything for the record). Only the description belongs on the publish card, so the
engine cuts it out of the file by the two banner lines below, and this file is the
only place those banners are spelled.
WHY THIS IS A JSON FILE AND NOT A LIST OF SPELLINGS IN THE PARSER. On 4 Sep 2026
the reader matched ANY line that began with the word DESCRIPTION or NOTES. The
writer had never been told to emit banners at all, so for eight episodes running it
latched onto whatever it found: EP38 and EP40-44 got the WHOLE FILE (thousands of
words of notes glued onto the description on the publish card); EP39 and EP45 got a
fragment of the notes, mid-sentence, because a sentence in the notes happened to
begin with the word DESCRIPTION. The rail's 1000-character floor caught EP45 by
luck and passed EP39 by luck. A check that only catches one shape of a fault is
the shape of failure this studio keeps meeting.
So the writer (docs/youtube-metadata-kit.md, File layout) and the reader
(engine/providers.py pasteable_description) both take the banners from HERE. A line
is a banner only when the WHOLE line is the banner text - not when it starts with
the same word. Change the form here and both sides change together, or neither does;
engine/test_youtube_copy_banners.py fails if the kit and this file disagree.
The fence characters either side of a banner, its spacing, its case and which dash a
keyboard produced are all forgiven when matching. The WORDS are not.
min_description_chars mirrors the rail's own floor in
supabase/migration-005-web-addresses.sql (length(new.youtube_copy) < 1000 is
refused). The parser enforces it first so the failure is named for what it is - a
layout fault in the file - rather than surfacing as a database error three retries
later. The same test checks the two numbers agree.
The layout, top to bottom (the kit shows it with prose around it):
1  the decided title, alone
2  (blank)
3  <description_banner>
4  <rule>
5  (blank)
6  the description, everything a human pastes, hashtags last
(blank)
<rule>
<notes_banner>
<rule>
(blank)
the notes
If you edit the banners here you are changing what every future -youtube.txt must
carry, and what every earlier one is read by.
notes_banner: NOTES — for the record, not for pasting
